name: Genetic Renal or Urinary Tract Malformation
aliases: Congenital Anomalies of the Kidney and Urinary Tract (CAKUT)

criteria.description: Presence of structural abnormalities of the kidney detected by prenatal or postnatal imaging
Hydronephrosis or ureteral dilation identified on ultrasound or other imaging modalities
Positive family history of renal or urinary tract malformations
Identification of pathogenic variants in known CAKUT-associated genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of at least one major structural renal or urinary tract anomaly on imaging with or without genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory; diagnosis is primarily based on imaging findings.

searchTerms: absent kidney on one or both sides
fluid buildup in kidney before birth

common.symptomName: Urinary tract infections secondary to malformation
searchTerms: repeated bladder infections from structural problems
UTIs caused by urinary tract abnormalities

common.symptomName: Impaired renal function in infancy or childhood
searchTerms: impaired renal function early in life
high blood pressure from small kidneys

occasional.symptomName: Growth retardation due to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: growth delay due to chronic kidney problems
failure to thrive related to kidney issues
underdeveloped lungs due to low amniotic fluid

rare.symptomName: Congenital heart defects associated with syndromic forms
Sensorineural hearing loss in syndromic cases

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine in cases with impaired renal function
Urine culture positive in recurrent urinary tract infections
imaging: Prenatal and postnatal renal ultrasound showing structural anomalies
Magnetic resonance urography for detailed urinary tract anatomy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as PAX2, HNF1B, EYA1, and RET
Familial segregation of mutations in affected families
other: Family history of renal or urinary tract malformations
Associated syndromic features in some cases (e.g., branchio-oto-renal syndrome)

distinguishingFeatures: Multiple bilateral renal cysts on imaging
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Obstructive uropathy with characteristic findings on voiding cystourethrogram

redFlags: Oligohydramnios detected prenatally indicating severe renal impairment
Progressive renal insufficiency in infancy or early childhood
Recurrent febrile urinary tract infections with structural abnormalities
references: Orphanet: Genetic Renal or Urinary Tract Malformation - ORPHA:183539
Sanna-Cherchi S, et al. Genetic basis of congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract. Nat Rev Nephrol. 2018.
